question:
A 28-year-old man with schizophrenia presents for a follow-up visit. Six months ago, he was
hospitalized and treated for a psychotic episode, with a prior episode occurring three years earlier. He
is currently undergoing weekly cognitive behavioral therapy and takes risperidone as his only
medication. He lives with his mother and two younger siblings, works 20 hours per week at a fast food
restaurant, smokes one pack of cigarettes daily, and consumes two to three beers daily. He denies
illicit drug use. On examination, he appears stable with normal vital signs and no physical
abnormalities. Mental status evaluation reveals a neutral affect, self-reported “decent” mood, organized
thought processes, normal attention and concentration, and intact memory. He successfully performs
serial sevens and a digit span test. Which of the following interventions is most appropriate to reduce
the likelihood of hospital readmission for his condition? Answer Choices: (A) Medication adherence
monitoring (B) Assertive community treatment (C) Psychoeducation for the patient only (D) Group
therapy focused on substance use (E) Mindfulness-based stress reduction therapy (F) Cognitive
remediation therapy (G) Social skills training (H) Exposure and response prevention therapy (I)
Long-acting injectable antipsychotic medication (J) Family therapy
 A. Medication adherence monitoring
B. Psychoeducation for the patient only
C. Assertive community treatment
D. Exposure and response prevention therapy
E. Family therapy
F. Social skills training
G. Cognitive remediation therapy
H. Group therapy focused on substance use
I. Long-acting injectable antipsychotic medication
J. Mindfulness-based stress reduction therapy
